documents.title: Electrophysiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Electrophysiology clinic, 01/10/2024.
Twelve weeks after CTI ablation for typical flutter. No palpitations since the procedure; breathing much better, back to walking 3 miles. No bleeding on apixaban.
ECG: sinus rhythm at 62.
Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, apixaban 5 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. NKDA.
Assessment: typical atrial flutter, successfully ablated, no recurrence.
Plan: stop apixaban today. Continue metoprolol until the repeat echo next month. EP follow-up as needed.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness. LVEF 55% by biplane method; no regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal. Trileaflet aortic valve with moderate aortic regurgitation, unchanged from 03/2023. No aortic stenosis. Other valves without significant abnormality. Ascending aorta 4.5 cm. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Recovered LV function, LVEF 55%, normal LV size. Moderate aortic regurgitation, unchanged. Ascending aorta 4.5 cm.

Cardiology follow-up 02/13/2024.
Feels well, exercising, no dyspnea or palpitations. Echo today: LV back to normal size, EF 55%; moderate AR unchanged; ascending aorta 4.5 cm.
Impression: tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy with recovered EF after flutter ablation. Moderate AR and 4.5 cm ascending aneurysm, stable.
Plan: stop metoprolol. Continue lisinopril 20 and hydrochlorothiazide 25; BP goal under 130/80. Surveillance echo and aortic imaging in 12 months. NKDA.

documents.title: Fatigue, supraclavicular node
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
49M. Off metoprolol 2 wks per cardiology, EF recovered. Here for a month of tiredness that keeps getting worse, worse than when his heart was racing; and a painless lump above the left collarbone he found shaving in late January. Not getting smaller. No fevers, no night sweats, no weight loss, no itch, no cough. No recent infections.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. NKDA.

Exam: BP 148/64, HR 65, afebrile, weight stable. Left supraclavicular node about 3 cm, firm, rubbery, nontender, not fixed. No cervical, axillary or inguinal nodes. No hepatosplenomegaly palpable (flanks full from his kidneys as before). Heart: diastolic murmur LSB, regular. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Left supraclavicular node, 3 cm, with fatigue - needs tissue. CBC w diff, CMP, LDH today. CXR today. Urgent heme/onc referral; called their intake line myself.
2. HTN - systolic up today, likely anxiety; recheck next visit.
Will call with results.

documents.title: Urgent referral to hematology/oncology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: URGENT referral: Hematology/Oncology. 49M, 3 cm firm nontender left supraclavicular node for about a month with progressive fatigue; no B symptoms. CBC normal, LDH 312. CXR today: no mediastinal widening or lung lesion. PMH: ADPKD, HTN, moderate AR/ascending aortic aneurysm 4.5 cm, atrial flutter s/p ablation with recovered EF. Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. NKDA. Please see for tissue diagnosis.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Glenn: blood counts and CMP normal. LDH 312, above normal. Chest x-ray: no widening of the middle of the chest and no lung spots. Explained the node still needs to be sampled and the LDH supports seeing oncology soon. Heme/onc has him 3/25 - asked to be put on the cancellation list. He is anxious; wife will go with him.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology consultation
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Outside cancer center - Hematology/Oncology New Patient Consultation
Date of visit: 03/25/2024

Referred by primary care for a left supraclavicular node.

HPI: 49-year-old man with ADPKD and hypertension, recently treated for atrial flutter with a rate-related cardiomyopathy (EF now recovered), with two months of steadily worsening fatigue and a painless lump in the left lower neck. He denies fevers, drenching sweats and weight loss.

PMH: ADPKD; hypertension; psychogenic erectile dysfunction; adjustment disorder; aortic regurgitation; tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; lisinopril per patient. NKDA.
Family history: father ADPKD/ESRD at 62; paternal grandfather ruptured cerebral aneurysm at 58; mother hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol, senior operations manager.

Exam: firm, nontender 3 cm lymph node in the left supraclavicular fossa. No other lymphadenopathy. Remainder of the exam unremarkable.

Data: CBC within normal limits. LDH 296, elevated (312 last month). HIV antigen/antibody negative. Chest radiograph 02/27: no mediastinal widening, no lung lesions.

Assessment: isolated supraclavicular adenopathy with elevated LDH; lymphoma is the leading concern.

Plan: excisional biopsy of the node (surgical oncology next week). If lymphoma is confirmed, PET/CT for staging. Will update primary care.

events.reason: excisional biopsy, left supraclavicular lymph node

reports.text:
Specimen: left supraclavicular lymph node, excision.
Gross: a 3.1 x 2.6 x 2.0 cm tan-pink lymph node.
Microscopic: nodal architecture effaced by closely packed neoplastic follicles composed of centrocytes with 6 to 15 centroblasts per high-power field. No diffuse large-cell areas identified.
Immunohistochemistry: neoplastic cells positive for CD20, CD10, BCL2 and BCL6; CD5 negative. Ki-67 approximately 20%.
Flow cytometry: CD10-positive monoclonal B-cell population, lambda light chain restricted.
reports.conclusion: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: follicular lymphoma, grade 2 (WHO grade 1-2), left supraclavicular lymph node.

documents.title: Operative note: lymph node excision
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Outpatient surgery - Operative Note
Date: 04/02/2024
Procedure: excisional biopsy, left supraclavicular lymph node.
Anesthesia: general (LMA).
Findings: single 3 cm firm node in the left supraclavicular fossa, removed intact and sent fresh for pathology and flow cytometry.
EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day. NKDA.

documents.title: Pathology reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Node pathology: follicular lymphoma, grade 2. Oncology has the result and has him for PET and a treatment discussion. Called Glenn; he had heard from oncology already. Offered support, will touch base after his oncology visit.

reports.text:
FDG PET/CT, skull base to mid-thigh. Fasting glucose acceptable.
Neck: FDG-avid soft tissue in the left supraclavicular surgical bed. No other cervical nodes.
Chest: no avid mediastinal or hilar nodes. Lungs clear. Heart normal size.
Abdomen/pelvis: multiple FDG-avid para-aortic lymph nodes, the largest 2.2 cm short axis, and FDG-avid bilateral common iliac nodes up to 1.8 cm. Liver and spleen normal in size with physiologic uptake. Both kidneys enlarged and polycystic, without abnormal uptake. No abnormal marrow uptake.
reports.conclusion: FDG-avid lymphoma above and below the diaphragm: left supraclavicular, para-aortic and bilateral common iliac nodes. No organ or marrow involvement. Findings positive for distant disease.

documents.title: Oncology treatment plan
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Hematology/Oncology follow-up 04/16/2024.
Pathology: follicular lymphoma, grade 2. PET/CT 04/09: FDG-avid disease in the left supraclavicular region and in para-aortic and bilateral common iliac nodes; no extranodal or marrow involvement. Stage III.
He remains fatigued; no B symptoms. LDH elevated at diagnosis. Hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody negative.
Assessment: stage III follicular lymphoma, grade 2, symptomatic, with elevated LDH - treatment indicated.
Plan: bendamustine and rituximab every 28 days for 6 cycles, starting 04/30. Chose a regimen without an anthracycline given his recent cardiomyopathy. Counts and chemistry with each cycle. Avoid live vaccines during and after therapy; inactivated flu and COVID vaccines are fine. End-of-treatment PET after cycle 6.
Discussed goals: high likelihood of a long remission. He and his wife asked good questions.

documents.title: Check-in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Glenn after oncology's note. Follicular lymphoma, stage III; starting BR on 4/30. He's taking it in stride, more worried about work coverage than the treatment. Sleeping ok. Told him to keep us in the loop and to call for anything between oncology visits, including blood pressure or mood. Will see him mid-treatment.

documents.title: Follow-up during chemotherapy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Between cycles 4 and 5 of BR. Tired for a few days after each cycle then recovers; no infections. Working mostly remote. Appetite fine, weight down a kg. Mood ok, PHQ-2 1.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. Off metoprolol and apixaban since winter. NKDA.
Exam: BP 134/72, HR 70. Well appearing, no thrush. No palpable left supraclavicular node, scar healed. Diastolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P
1. Follicular lymphoma on BR, tolerating. Oncology following labs.
2. HTN - acceptable, near goal; continue.
3. AR/aortic aneurysm - cardiology surveillance due Feb/Mar.
4. Vaccines: inactivated flu and updated COVID this fall are fine; Shingrix and pneumococcal after he finishes chemo.
RTC January.

reports.text:
FDG PET/CT, skull base to mid-thigh, compared with 04/09/2024.
No residual FDG-avid disease. Previously avid left supraclavicular, para-aortic and common iliac nodes have resolved, residual para-aortic nodes subcentimeter without uptake above background. Liver and spleen normal. Polycystic kidneys unchanged. Marrow uptake diffuse and physiologic.

documents.title: End of treatment
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Hematology/Oncology, 10/15/2024.
Completed 6 cycles of bendamustine-rituximab 09/17/2024. Energy improving. No nodes on exam. CBC recovering; LDH 201, normal.
PET/CT 10/08: complete metabolic response.
Assessment: stage III follicular lymphoma, grade 2, in complete remission after BR.
Plan: no maintenance therapy. Surveillance visits every 6 months for 2 years with exam, CBC and LDH; imaging only for symptoms. Recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccination may proceed from January. NKDA.

documents.title: End-of-treatment results reviewed

documents.body: Oncology letter and PET reviewed: complete metabolic response after 6 cycles BR. Surveillance with oncology every 6 months. Due here in January for Shingrix and PCV20.
